claims.text: A phospholipid has a polar, hydrophilic head that contains a phosphate group, and two non-polar, hydrophobic fatty acid tails; glycerol joins the head to the tails, but it is the phosphate group that makes the head polar. In water the molecules form a bilayer with the heads facing outwards towards the water on both sides and the tails facing inwards, away from it.

claims.text: Cholesterol sits among the fatty acid tails and regulates the fluidity of the membrane: at warm temperatures it tends to restrict the movement of the tails, making the membrane more stable, and at low temperatures it tends to stop the tails packing closely, so the membrane does not become stiff; it also tends to reduce leakage of ions and small polar molecules between the phospholipids.
